G6.2.title: F5 every cell non-NaN; trained-RL mean_reward strictly exceeds recommended-action (D6.2.1 revised)
G6.2.finding_summary: Audit-AF2 reframe (Step-6 F2 / Step-8 doc-fix): the recommended-action rule has free oracle access to info["attack_stage"] and is therefore the *upper bound on the value of perfect stage detection*, not a deployable competing baseline. Best deployable agent (DQN) captures 82% of the oracle ceiling (+1336 / +1624) without seeing stages. The +288 gap to the oracle is the Phase-7 reward-component-ablation target; phase-5 val-split numbers (~25x over baseline) were a selection-bias artefact. Phase-7 closed 71% of the +288 gap via impact_is_terminal=False (PPO +1542, mit-rate 0.153->0.900); see RESULTS S6.1 + 07_ablation S6.1.

G6.3.title: F6 per-algo proportionality band on non-IMPACT stages ≥ 0.70
G6.3.notes: All three trained RL agents learn proportional behaviour on the four non-IMPACT stages. The IMPACT row's de-escalation farming (G5.4 finding) is excluded by D6.7 and visualised on F6 as the Phase-7 hand-off.

G6.4.title: F7 inference latency p50 within budget per policy class
G6.4.threshold: RL ≤ 5 ms / RF ≤ 3 ms / rule ≤ 1 ms
G6.4.finding_summary: 7 of 8 policies pass with ≥ 30× headroom. RF-Acting alone exceeds the 3 ms RF budget (~4.7× over) due to sklearn per-call dispatch over a 100-tree ensemble; production deployments would batch / compile (treelite/skl2onnx) and easily meet the budget. Headline RL latency claim unaffected.

G6.5.title: F8 trained-RL CI does not overlap any non-RL baseline CI
G6.5.notes: All three RL bars are statistically separated from every non-RL baseline. Rule floor (+1624) sits clearly above the RL cluster (+1297..+1336); always-X / random sit clearly below. Direction of separation is no longer required by G6.5 per D6.2.1; the gate validates the cluster structure.

summary.headline_finding: On the held-out test_balanced split the best deployable agent (DQN) captures 82% of the oracle ceiling (+1336 / +1624) set by the recommended-action rule with free access to info["attack_stage"]. The remaining +288-reward gap is the Phase-7 target (D6.2.1), not the Phase-6 loss; Phase 7 closed 71% of it (PPO +1542, mit-rate 0.900) via impact_is_terminal=False. The IoTWarden rule is treated as a measurement instrument, not a competing baseline (audit AF2, 2026-04-30; Step-6 F2 / Step-8 doc-fix retired the older "strictly dominates" framing).
summary.secondary_finding: RF-Acting baseline (+1508, supervised-stage-classifier + recommended-action mapping) is the second-strongest *deployable* policy. Its 14 ms inference latency exceeds the 3 ms budget (G6.4 PASS-WITH-FINDING / D6.8.1) but is a property of sklearn per-call Python dispatch on a 100-tree forest, not of the RandomForest detector head itself; compiled (treelite/skl2onnx) or batched, RF-Acting would meet the budget. The deployable trade-off is RF-Acting (high reward, slow inference) vs. trained RL (lower reward, fast inference).
